records.Short Business Description: Nasdaq, Inc. operates as a technology company that serves capital markets and other industries in the United States and internationally.
records.Long Business Description:
Nasdaq, Inc. (Nasdaq) operates as a technology platform that powers the world’s economies.

The company empowers economic opportunity by designing and deploying technology, data, and advanced analytics that enable the company’s clients to capture opportunities, navigate risk, and strengthen resilience.

The company manages, operates, and provides its products and services in three business segments: Capital Access Platforms, Financial Technology, and Market Services.

The company’s transformation into a leading technology platform that powers the world’s economies gained momentum with the 2021 acquisition of Verafin, followed by the 2023 acquisition of Adenza and its two flagship solutions, AxiomSL, and Calypso.

Growth Strategy

The company’s strategies are to advance economic progress for all, and deliver world-leading platforms that advance the liquidity, transparency, and integrity of the global economy.

Products and Services

Capital Access Platforms

The company’s Capital Access Platforms segment delivers liquidity, transparency, and integrity to the corporate issuer and investment community by empowering its clients to effectively navigate the capital markets, achieve their sustainability goals, and drive governance excellence. The company offers a suite of products to assist companies in managing corporate governance standards.

The company’s Capital Access Platforms segment comprises Data & Listing Services, Index, and Workflow & Insights.

Data & Listing Services

The company’s North American and European data products enhance transparency of market activity within its exchanges, and provide critical information to professional and non-professional investors globally. The company’s Data business distributes historical and real-time market data to sell-side customers, the institutional investing community, retail online brokers, proprietary trading firms, and other venues, as well as internet portals and data distributors.

The company collects, processes, and creates information, and earns revenues as a distributor of its own, as well as select third-party, content. The company provides varying levels of quote and trade information to market participants, and to data distributors who in turn provide subscriptions for this information. The company’s systems enable distributors to gain access to its market depth, order imbalances, market sentiment, and other analytical data.

The company distributes this proprietary market information to both market participants and non-participants through a number of proprietary products, including Nasdaq TotalView, the company’s flagship market depth quote product. The company offers TotalView products for The Nasdaq Stock Market, and its Nasdaq BX and Nasdaq PSX markets. The company also offers Nordic Equity TotalView, Nordic Derivatives TotalView, and Nordic Fixed Income TotalView for Nordic markets.

The company operates several other proprietary services and data products to provide market information, including Nasdaq Basic, a lower cost alternative to the industry Level 1 feed, and Nasdaq Canada Basic, a lower cost alternative to other data feeds. The company also provides various other data, including data relating to its U.S. equities and options exchanges, and Nordic equities, derivatives, fixed income, and futures.

The company operates a variety of listing platforms around the world to provide multiple global capital raising solutions for public companies. Companies listed on the company’s markets represent a diverse array of industries, including, among others, healthcare, consumer products, telecommunication services, information technology, financial services, industrials, and energy. The company’s main listing markets are The Nasdaq Stock Market, and the Nasdaq Nordic and Nasdaq Baltic exchanges.

Companies seeking to list securities on The Nasdaq Stock Market may do so on one of the three market tiers: The Nasdaq Global Select Market, The Nasdaq Global Market, or The Nasdaq Capital Market. To qualify, companies must meet minimum listing requirements, including specified financial and corporate governance criteria. Once listed, companies must maintain rigorous listing and corporate governance standards.

As of December 31, 2025, a total of 5,599 companies listed securities on the company’s U.S., Nasdaq Nordic, Nasdaq Baltic, and Nasdaq First North exchanges. As of December 31, 2025, a total of 4,480 companies listed securities on The Nasdaq Stock Market, with 1,316 listings on The Nasdaq Global Select Market, 1,750 on The Nasdaq Global Market, and 1,414 on The Nasdaq Capital Market.

In the U.S., the company seeks new listings from companies conducting IPOs, including SPACs, and direct listings, as well as companies looking to switch from alternative exchanges.

During 2025, the company had 20 new listings resulting from operating companies switching their listings from NYSE or NYSE American to join The Nasdaq Stock Market, as well as 5 ETP switches.

The company also offers listings on the exchanges that comprise Nasdaq Nordic and Nasdaq Baltic. For smaller companies and growth companies, the company offers access to the financial markets through the Nasdaq First North alternative marketplaces. As of December 31, 2025, a total of 1,119 companies listed securities on the company’s Nordic and Baltic exchanges.

The company’s European listing customers include companies, funds, and governments. Customers issue securities in the form of cash equities, depository receipts, warrants, ETPs, convertibles, rights, options, bonds, or fixed-income related products. In 2025, a total of 27 new companies listed on its Nordic and Baltic exchanges.

Index

The company’s Index business develops and licenses Nasdaq-branded indices and financial products. License fees for the company’s trademark licenses vary by product based on a percentage of underlying assets, dollar value of a product issuance, number of products, or number of contracts traded. The company also licenses cash-settled options, futures, and options on futures on its indices.

As of December 31, 2025, 451 ETPs listed on 27 exchanges in over 20 countries tracked a Nasdaq index. The company’s flagship index, the Nasdaq-100 Index, or NDX, includes the top 100 non-financial companies listed on The Nasdaq Stock Market.

The company provides index data products based on Nasdaq indices. Index data products include its Global Index Data Service, which delivers real-time and historical index values throughout the trading day, and Global Index Watch/Global Index File Delivery Service, which delivers daily and historical weightings and components data, corporate actions, and a breadth of additional data for the indices that the company operates.

Workflow & Insights

Workflow & Insights includes the company’s analytics and corporate solutions products.

The company’s analytics products provide asset managers, investment consultants, and institutional asset owners with information and analytics to make data-driven investment decisions, deploy their resources more productively, and provide liquidity solutions for private funds. Through the company’s eVestment platform, it provides a suite of cloud-based solutions that help institutional investors and consultants conduct pre-investment due diligence, and monitor their portfolios post-investment. The eVestment platform also enables asset managers to efficiently distribute information about their firms and funds to asset owners and consultants worldwide. The company’s eVestment platform has expanded the scale and reach of data assets to meet the evolving needs of clients, and enhance the value to asset owners and asset managers, including in the private markets space, with over 80,000 private funds covered. In October 2025, the company sold its Solovis business, a financial technology platform offering portfolio monitoring and analytics tools.

records.Long Business Description:
Nextdoor Holdings, Inc. (Nextdoor) operates a neighborhood network.

The company is connecting over 105 million Verified Neighbors to the people, places, and information that matter most in their local communities. Operating in over 350,000 neighborhoods across 11 countries, Nextdoor fosters trusted, real-world utility through locally relevant content and services, including news, real-time safety alerts, neighbor recommendations, for sale and free listings, and events. This focus on practical local value drives genuine, high-intent local engagement and supports a diverse ecosystem of neighbors and partners seeking to connect with neighbors.

The company’s platform is powered by unique geospatial technology and a proprietary advertising system that enables businesses of all sizes to reach highly engaged audiences with a local focus. Through these capabilities, Nextdoor helps strengthen local communities while providing partners — including small businesses, national brands, publishers, and civic and government agencies — with effective tools to communicate and engage locally at scale.

As of December 31, 2025, Nextdoor had 21.0 million Platform Weekly Active Users (‘Platform WAU’) and reached 1 in 3 households in the United States.

The company’s Platform and The company’s Users

In 2025, the company launched the new Nextdoor initiative, the first phase of a multi-phase product transformation designed to create more engaging experiences for neighbors and partners and deliver enhanced value for advertisers. This evolution expands the platform beyond primarily neighbor-generated content to a dynamic feed enriched with timely, locally relevant information — including news and alerts — with artificial intelligence (‘AI’) and machine learning (‘ML’) used to help surface and personalize content for neighbors.

The Nextdoor Ecosystem

Nextdoor is built on the unique combination of neighbor identity, trust and proximity. The company’s platform is powered by the company’s core constituencies: neighbors, businesses, and public agencies seeking to build stronger, more connected communities. Neighbors use Nextdoor to connect with their neighbors, follow local news, participate in conversations, discover and support local businesses, and exchange goods and services. Businesses use the company’s platform to reach high-intent audiences through free Business Pages and targeted advertising, while public agencies — including fire departments, law enforcement, and municipal offices — share real-time updates, critical alerts, and community information.

This ecosystem is further enhanced by more than 4,000 local news publishers whose content accounted, as of December 31, 2025, for approximately 7% of total feed volume, as well as alert partners, such as Waze, Weather.com, and the U.S. Geological Survey. These partnerships deliver real-time traffic, weather, and safety notifications, increasing the relevance and utility of the company’s platform.

Advertising Solutions

Nextdoor offers a comprehensive suite of advertising solutions designed to deliver measurable results for businesses of all sizes. The company’s Nextdoor Ads Platform is built on a proprietary ad stack that includes the Nextdoor Ads Manager interface, the company’s native ad server, and measurement and API tools. Together, these capabilities help businesses to connect with high-intent local audiences, build brand awareness, and drive customer engagement where decisions are made: in the neighborhood.

Go-to-Market Approach

The company’s go-to-market approach combines the scale and efficiency of the company’s self-serve ads platform with the expertise of a dedicated global sales team. This hybrid approach allows the company to cater to businesses of all sizes, from small local businesses to large global brands, across both self-serve and managed campaigns. In addition to buying directly through the company’s platform, advertisers can work with select programmatic and data partners to reach Nextdoor audiences more efficiently using their existing programmatic workflows.

Nextdoor Ads Manager (‘NAM’) is the primary interface to the company’s proprietary ad stack and powers the company’s self-serve advertising channel by enabling advertisers to independently plan, launch, and optimize campaigns. Continued product investments in automated optimization, AI-driven creative support, and simplified campaign management have delivered measurable performance improvements, including higher click-through rates and lower cost-per-click for advertisers.

For advertisers with more complex needs, the company’s dedicated global sales team provides personalized support across the company’s ad stack throughout the marketing lifecycle, including campaign planning, optimization, and performance analysis. Strategically positioned across markets, the company’s sales team focuses on attracting and retaining advertisers while driving measurable outcomes across all ad products.

A Community First Approach

Nextdoor continually innovates to facilitate productive neighborhood conversations. The company maintains this constructive and authentic environment through a multi-layered strategy that combines neighbor verification based on location with clear Community Guidelines, and a hybrid moderation model leveraging both advanced technology and human review.

Real Identity and Verification

To ensure authenticity, Nextdoor requires neighbors to sign up using their real names and addresses. This verification process creates a network of real people, establishing a foundation of trust. Businesses, news partners, and public agencies undergo a similar verification process to establish trust within the ecosystem.

Hybrid Moderation Framework

The company employs a three-tiered moderation framework to maintain a positive and productive environment.

AI and Automated Solutions: The company utilize ML models to proactively detect and flag harmful content before it is visible. Features, such as the Kindness Reminder and Constructive Conversations Reminder encourage respectful dialogue by analyzing tone and suggesting constructive edits. From time to time, the company tests generative AI tools, including tools intended to help neighbors draft more constructive and engaging posts and comments in line with the company’s Community Guidelines.

Community Moderation: Leveraging the local context known by the company’s users, the company supports a network of over 200,000 volunteer community reviewers. These volunteer neighbor reviewers are equipped with specialized tools to review reported content and uphold Community Guidelines in a way that reflects the unique nuances of their neighborhoods.

Neighborhood Operations Team: Reports of specific types of content, including misinformation and discrimination, are escalated directly to Nextdoor’s internal operations staff. This ensures consistent, professional enforcement of the company’s standards and policies.

Focus on Engagement Quality

The company intends to balance high-quality interactions on its platform with growth in overall usage. From time to time, the company adjusts its notification and email strategies, including periods where the company reduce or reconfigure volume to improve relevance and the overall neighbor experience. These changes, together with product experiments, seasonality, and other factors, can lead to fluctuations in available ad impressions and short-term metrics, such as Platform WAU. Over the long term, focusing on relevant, useful experiences for neighbors is important to sustaining trust, deepening engagement, and supporting the company’s business.

records.Long Business Description:
NFT Limited, through its subsidiaries, operates an electronic online platform for artists, art dealers, and art investors to offer and trade in ownership over valuable artwork in the form of non-fungible token or NFT.

The company offers online listing and trading services that allow artists, art dealers and owners to access a much bigger art trading market where they can engage with a wide range of investors that they might not encounter without its platform. The company’s platform also makes investment in high-end and expensive artwork more accessible to ordinary people without substantial financial resources. The company also provides NFT consulting with respect to the strategic utilization of blockchain technology and NFT launch. The company is also exploring NFT gaming business, including sales of in-game characters NFTs and sales of membership packs.

The company offers online listing and trading services that allow artists/art dealers/owners to access a much bigger art trading market where they can engage with a wide range of investors that they might not encounter without its platform. The company’s platform also invests in high-end and expensive artwork more accessible to ordinary people without substantial financial resources.

The company, through its operating subsidiaries, generate revenue from services in connection with the offering and trading of artwork on its system, primarily consisting of trading commissions on the listing and trading of NFTs on its platform.

Takung Digital Technology Limited (Takung Digital) is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the company. This entity primarily provides administrative and technical supports for the development of NFT projects.

Takung Exchange Limited (Takung Exchange) is wholly owned by the company. This entity facilitates the business and operation of the new Takung Exchange market.

Metaverse Digital Payment Co., Limited (Metaverse HK) is wholly owned by Takung Exchange. This entity engages in digital payment service.

Trading Platform

The company’s proprietary platform is an all-electronic trading system, consisting of host computers, client-side terminals and an interconnected communication system. The company’s trading system supports the trading and payment/settlement of artwork ownership units. It is an electronic platform developed by a third-party software development company and customized for it, primarily consisting of a matching system, a transaction monitoring system, an account managing system and a settlement system.

Matching is a core function of the company’s trading platform. The company’s system concludes transactions by matching all the transactions submitted by the Traders. Transaction monitoring system is responsible for monitoring the daily transactions in real-time to ensure fairness and accuracy in its trading platform. The settlement system verifies and reconciles daily statistical data with the banks’ transaction system, and completes the registration and settlement (or payment) of artwork units once the transaction data is verified. The company’s website https://www.nftoeo.com/ is an essential part of its trading platform.

The company’s website is important, as it serves as the gateway to its trading platform. It publishes its membership, and trading rules, trading information disclosure, and artwork introduction, and provides services to Traders, such as account management. Traders may open, close, and manage their accounts with the company on its website. The client-end terminal may be downloaded from its website. Through the terminal, Traders may access their accounts with the company, and conduct transactions in artwork units, such as purchasing, selling, and submitting inquiries. Data transmission between the Traders, and the company's trading system is encrypted to prevent data leaks.

In order to execute a trade, a Trader logs into his online bank account and must first transfer funds from his bank account to his trading account with the company.

The offering, and trading of artwork on the company’s platform involves a number of parties, namely, Original Owner, Offering Agent, and Traders.

An Original Owner is the original owner of the artwork to be offered, and traded on the company's platform. Customarily, the Original Owner is also the artist, or creator of the artwork, although this is not always the case. The Original Owner must have good, and marketable title to the artwork, and have the right to dispose of the artwork.

An Offering Agent is an entity that is experienced with artwork or artwork investment and has a good reputation. The Offering Agent is engaged by the Original Owner to assist him or her with the offering and trading of artwork, such as preparation of listing application and assigning an investment value, research, organizing promotions and marketing activities, communicating with potential investors, etc.

Additional parties, such as insurer, appraisal firm, trader service organizations, and custodian for artworks, will be retained in connection with the offering, and trading of artwork on the company's system. A trader service organization is an independent legal entity, pre-approved by the company, to provide business consulting services to its Traders.

The company's trading system hardware platform is hosted by a rendered service from Amazon Web, and its server is located in Singapore. Its clearing system hardware platform is hosted in Hong Kong, and its disaster recovery system is set up in the CITIC Telecom IDC room, located in Hong Kong. The real-time data synchronization ensures the safety of transaction data.

Revenue

The company generates revenue from its services in connection with the offering, and trading of artwork on its system. Its revenue is mainly generated from trading commissions.

Sales and Marketing

The company has a professional marketing team. After the platform is launched, it can be promoted online and offline simultaneously, so as to quickly increase its popularity, and use professional marketing solutions to attract more creators and purchasers to join the platform.

Supply of Services

The company provides a platform to trade in artwork units, for which it is compensated by receiving listing fees, management fees, and trading commissions. The Hong Kong Supply of Services (Implied Terms) Ordinance (SSO) provides that, in the absence of provisions in the contract for services, services should be carried out with reasonable care, and skill (which generally means the services must meet the standard that a reasonable person would regard as satisfactory) (section 5 of the SSO), the services should be performed within a reasonable time if the time of performance has not been fixed by the contract (section 6 of the SSO), and a reasonable charge should be paid if the charge has not been fixed by the contract (section 7 of the SSO).

Intellectual Property

In China, the Trademark Law and the Unfair Competition Law governs the company’s marks.

Employment

Some of its employees are employed in Hong Kong and the company is subject to the Hong Kong Employment Ordinance (EO). Other mandatory laws that are likely to apply to the employment relationship with the company’s employees include: Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (PDPO); Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Ordinance (MPFSO); Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (OSHO); Employees’ Compensation Ordinance (ECO); Companies Ordinance; Sex Discrimination Ordinance (SDO), Disability Discrimination Ordinance (DDO), Family Status Discrimination Ordinance (FSDO) and Race Discrimination Ordinance (RDO); Basic Law and the Hong Kong Bill of Rights Ordinance; Labour Tribunal Ordinance; and Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (POBO).

records.Short Business Description: Norwegian Block Exchange AS offers an internet-based marketplace for customers to buy and sell digital assets in Norway.
records.Long Business Description:
Norwegian Block Exchange AS (Norwegian Block Exchange) operates as a financial service company that specializes in developing digital asset-based products. It offers an internet-based marketplace for customers to buy and sell digital assets.

Business Segments

Norwegian Block Exchange’s operations are segmented into various core areas, which contribute to its overarching mission of bridging traditional finance and digital finance. The primary business segments include: Digital Asset Exchange, Tokenization Services, Custody Services, Credit Services, Compliance and Regulatory Services, and Software Development.

Digital Asset Exchange: This segment operates a cryptocurrency exchange, which facilitates the buying, selling, and trading of various digital assets. This segment serves both individual and institutional clients and aims to ensure user-friendly experiences alongside robust security protocols.

Tokenization Services: This segment specializes in tokenizing real-world assets, thereby allowing investors fractional ownership of high-value items. Recent projects include tokenizing precious stones for a partnership with The Mint. This segment also involves initiatives like SunSpearX, a joint venture to tokenize solar power installations.

Custody Services: This segment of the company’s partnership with AKJ enables them to offer custody-as-a-service, which is becoming increasingly important as regulation in cryptocurrency environments tightens. This service enhances the security and trust for institutional clients handling digital assets.

Credit Services: This segment of the company in 2023, launched the NBX Visa Credit Card, designed to facilitate transactions in cryptocurrencies while also rewarding customers with Bitcoin cashback. This segment has undergone significant development, including the integration of user-friendly features popular with current and prospective users.

Compliance and Regulatory Services: This segment focuses on ensuring compliance with regulatory frameworks. The company’s proactive stance on regulatory alignment fosters trust among users and investors.

Software Development: This segment invests in developing its trading platform and related technologies. This segment focuses on continuous enhancement both in functionality and user experience, contributing directly to operational performance and customer engagement.

Business Strategy

The business strategy of Norwegian Block Exchange pivots around the concept of being a full-fledged digital asset service provider bridging traditional and digital finance realms. Central to this strategy is the drive to offer comprehensive, secure, and regulated services to both retail and institutional customers. Key components of this strategy include:

Technology Innovation: Continuous investment in technology is vital to Norwegian Block Exchange. The development of a robust trading platform is essential to facilitate seamless transactions and an engaging user experience, which aligns with the growing expectations within the digital finance ecosystem.

Client-Centric Approach: Understanding customer needs drives product development and enhancement. The company places significant emphasis on customer feedback, facilitating tailored solutions that resonate with user requirements, fostering loyalty, and expanding its customer base.

Products and Services

The product and service offerings of Norwegian Block Exchange encompass a diverse range of digital asset solutions aimed at various customer segments:

Cryptocurrency Exchange: An intuitive interface designed for trading a variety of cryptocurrencies, ensuring liquidity and security for users. This service is foundational to Norwegian Block Exchange’s operation.

NBX Visa Credit Card: This newly launched service allows users to spend their cryptocurrency while earning Bitcoin cashback. Features such as Google Pay and Apple Pay integration enhance usability and attract additional customers.

Custody-as-a-Service: Tailored for institutional clients, this offering secures digital assets, ensuring they meet compliance and regulatory requirements.

Tokenization Services: Norwegian Block Exchange facilitates the digitization of real-world assets, enabling fractional ownership and investment opportunities for users via its marketplace.

Staking and Earning Programs: Customers can earn rewards by participating in staking programs, allowing them to take full advantage of their cryptocurrency holdings.

Geographical Markets Served

Norwegian Block Exchange primarily serves markets in Scandinavia, with potential outreach across the European Economic Area. The strategic regulations and partnerships established position the company favorably within European discussions surrounding cryptocurrency and digital asset trading.

Seasonality

Norwegian Block Exchange observes cyclical trends tied to cryptocurrency market fluctuations. The fluctuating nature of digital asset trading often correlates with broader economic indicators and market sentiments, rather than season-specific variables.

Customers

Norwegian Block Exchange serves a diverse customer base that includes individual investors, institutional clients, and corporate customers. The customer categories include retail cryptocurrency traders, businesses seeking tokenization services, and financial institutions leveraging custody services.

Sales and Marketing

Norwegian Block Exchange employs multifaceted sales and marketing strategies that encompass online marketing, strategic partnerships, and community engagements. The utilization of social media and industry events aids in fostering customer relationships and enhancing visibility. Digital platforms are leveraged for seamless transactions and customer education, ensuring the brand maintains a strong presence in a competitive market.

Government Regulations

Norwegian Block Exchange is subject to regulations imposed by the Norwegian Financial Supervisory Authority and broader EU regulations concerning digital assets. Compliance with these regulations is vital for operational legitimacy.

History

Norwegian Block Exchange AS was founded in 2018. The company was incorporated in 2018.

records.Short Business Description: NZX Limited operates a stock exchange in New Zealand.
records.Long Business Description:
NZX Limited is a financial services company situated in New Zealand, primarily focused on operating a securities exchange and providing various market support services. Its core operations include the management and oversight of capital markets, commodity trading, and funds management services.

The company is dedicated to enhancing the efficiency and transparency of these markets while fostering growth and innovation within the financial landscape. With a commitment to maintaining high standards of regulatory compliance and integrity, the company plays a pivotal role in safeguarding the interests of all market participants.

Business Segments

The company operates through various distinct business segments, each contributing to the overall value proposition of the company. The primary segments are as follows:

Capital Markets: This segment encompasses origination, secondary markets, and information services. In terms of origination, the company facilitates initial public offerings (IPOs) and issues equity and debt securities. Secondary markets involve trading activities conducted on the exchange, providing liquidity to investors. The Information Services part offers analytics, market data, and insights that help both issuers and investors make informed decisions.

Funds Management: Gathering momentum through its subsidiary Smartshares Limited, the funds management segment specializes in managing superannuation, KiwiSaver products, and Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). It provides comprehensive administration services to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements while delivering value to fund participants.

Wealth Technologies: Operated through NZX Wealth Technologies Limited, this segment offers an integrated platform designed for financial advisers and brokers to manage client investments. By streamlining operations and facilitating efficient portfolio management, this segment contributes significantly to the financial advisory ecosystem.

Corporate Services: This internal segment delivers critical support functions across all business units, including accommodation, legal, finance, IT, and human resource management. It ensures the seamless operation of various business departments and is essential for maintaining the company's operational integrity.

Regulation: The company’s regulatory arm, NZ RegCo, operates independently to perform all frontline regulatory functions. This structural separation ensures the company can uphold its regulatory responsibilities without conflicts of interest, thereby maintaining investor confidence and market integrity.

Each of these segments is aligned with the company’s overarching mission to provide a robust, transparent, and efficient marketplace that serves a wide range of customer needs, thereby propelling the growth of New Zealand's capital markets.

Business Strategy

The company aims to establish itself as a pivotal player in New Zealand's financial ecosystem. The company is committed to promoting innovation and efficiency in its operations, focusing on several strategic priorities. The emphasis on enhancing customer experience is paramount, with ongoing efforts to refine service delivery channels and tools that make market participation seamless.

Furthermore, the company concentrates on leveraging technology to upgrade its platforms, thereby increasing operational capabilities and streamlining processes. These technological advancements not only bolster market access but also improve the quality of services offered to clients. The company also aspires to strengthen its position within the regulatory framework, ensuring that all operational processes adhere to high standards of compliance and governance.

A significant part in its strategy involves fostering partnerships and collaborations within the financial market. By aligning its goals with those of various stakeholders—including issuers, brokers, and institutional investors—the company aims to create a collaborative environment that encourages growth and market resilience.

Products and Services

The company offers a wide array of products and services designed to meet the diverse requirements of its clientele, including investors, issuers, and financial intermediaries. The principal offerings include:

Equity and Debt Listings: The company facilitates the listing of companies on its exchange, providing entities with access to capital while offering investors an opportunity to participate in ownership.

Trading Services: The company supports trading in a variety of instruments, including stocks, bonds, and derivatives. The trading infrastructure is designed to provide transparency and efficiency, essential for maintaining market integrity.

Market Data and Insights: An offering of comprehensive market data services includes real-time trading data, historical analytics, and sector performance insights, enriching clients' understanding of market dynamics.

Funds Administration: Through its funds management services, the company provides administrative support, compliance services, and portfolio management for a variety of investment funds, including ETFs and KiwiSaver schemes.

Regulatory Service: NZ RegCo oversees compliance and regulatory activities, ensuring that all market participants adhere to laws and regulations governing capital markets.

Wealth Management Tools: The Wealth Technologies division offers a platform that enhances the operational efficiency for advisers and brokers, enabling them to manage client portfolios effectively in a compliant manner.

These product offerings showcase the company’s commitment to fostering a multifaceted financial ecosystem characterized by access, transparency, and innovation.

Geographical Markets Served

The company predominantly operates within New Zealand, which serves as its primary market. The company has also extended its reach beyond New Zealand, with growing interests in the United States and Australia, although these are elective markets compared to its home territory. The company’s strategic positioning in these geographical areas is driven by an overarching ambition to attract international listings and foster cross-border investment activities.

Customers

The company serves a diverse range of customers, including:

Institutional Investors: Offering tailored products and services for large-scale investors.

Retail Investors: Facilitating access to a range of investment vehicles for individual investors.

Listed Entities: Supporting organizations that utilize the exchange for capital raising.

Financial Intermediaries: Providing tools and operational platforms for brokers and advisers.

Modes of Sales and Marketing

The company's marketing strategies encompass a multi-channel approach, integrating digital platforms, traditional marketing, and stakeholder engagement initiatives. Promotional activities include investor relations programs, public relations campaigns, and thought leadership through market insights, designed to elevate the NZX brand within the financial services landscape.

Government Regulations

The company operates under a stringent framework of government regulations that govern capital markets in New Zealand. This includes compliance with the Financial Markets Conduct Act and other applicable laws. The regulatory arm, NZ RegCo, plays a pivotal role in ensuring adherence to these legal requirements, thus promoting transparency and confidence in the financial markets.

History

The company was founded in 1866. It was incorporated in 2002. The company was formerly known as New Zealand Exchange Limited and changed its name to NZX Limited in July 2008.

The Secondary Markets segment provides trading and post-trade services for securities and derivatives markets, as well as provides central securities depository; and acts as a market operator for Fonterra Co-Operative Group, the Electricity Authority, and the Ministry for the Environment. The Information Services segment provides information services for the securities and derivatives markets, and analytics for the dairy sector. The Funds Management segment manages funds, such as KiwiSaver, superannuation, managed funds, and exchange traded funds. The Wealth Technologies segment provides funds administration and custodian services. The company was formerly known as New Zealand Exchange Limited and changed its name to NZX Limited in July 2008. records.Short Business Description: Open Lending Corporation provides lending enablement and risk analytics solutions to credit unions, regional banks, finance companies, and captive finance companies of automakers in the United States.
records.Long Business Description:
Open Lending Corporation (Open Lending) is a provides lending enablement and risk analytics services to credit unions, regional banks, finance companies, and the captive finance companies of automakers.

Through its flagship product, LPP, the company’s customers, collectively referred to as automotive lenders or lenders, make automotive consumer loans to underserved near-prime and non-prime borrowers by harnessing its risk-based interest rate pricing models, powered by proprietary data and real-time underwriting of automotive loan default insurance coverage from insurers. The company currently serves 450 active lenders.

Lenders Protection Platform (LPP)

LPP is a cloud-based automotive lending enablement platform that supports loans made to near-prime and non-prime borrowers. It is designed to underwrite default insurance by linking automotive lenders to the company’s insurance partners. The platform employs risk-based pricing models, enabling automotive lenders to assess the credit risk of potential borrowers using data-driven analysis. The company's proprietary risk models project loan performance, including expected losses and prepayments, to determine the optimal contract interest rate. LPP recommends a risk-based, all-inclusive interest rate for a loan, customized to each automotive lender, reflecting cost of capital, loan servicing and acquisition costs, expected recovery rates, and target return on assets. These risk models utilize a proprietary score that combines credit bureau data and Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA)-compliant alternative consumer data to effectively assess risk and determine the appropriate insurance premium for any given loan application.

LPP is powered by technology that delivers speed and scalability in providing interest rate decisioning to automotive lenders. It supports the full transaction lifecycle, including credit application, underwriting, real-time insurance approval, settlement, servicing, invoicing of insurance premiums and fees, and advanced data analytics of the automotive lender’s portfolio under the program. Through electronic system integration, the company's software technology connects it to parties within its ecosystem.

A key element of LPP is the unique database that drives risk decisioning using data accumulated for approximately 25 years. When a loan is insured at origination, all attributes of the transaction are stored in the company's database. Through the claims management process, the company ultimately obtains loan life performance data on each insured loan. Granular origination and performance data enable the company's data scientists and actuaries to evolve and refine risk models based on actual experience and third-party information sources.

Business Model

The company specializes in risk-based pricing and modeling, providing automated decision-technology for automotive lenders throughout the U.S. LPP targets the financing needs of near-prime and non-prime borrowers, or borrowers with a credit bureau score generally between 560 and 699, who are underserved in the automotive finance industry. The company aims to make this market more competitive, resulting in more attractive loan terms.

Operating under a business-to-business model, the company’s customers are automotive lenders. LPP enables automotive lenders to expand their lending guidelines to offer loans to borrowers with lower credit bureau scores, potentially leading to increased loan originations and higher loan advance rates. LPP integrates directly with automotive lenders’ existing loan origination systems, facilitating electronic delivery of all-inclusive loan rates in real-time to automotive lenders. Designed to provide real-time experience, LPP is intuitive and easy to use.

The company has exclusivity agreements with insurance partners who provide default insurance to automotive lenders on individual automotive loans processed through LPP, which underwrites the risk on each loan application. Insurance partners issue default insurance to the company’s customers, creating a direct contractual relationship between the insurer and the lender. Loan applications are allocated to insurance partners based on pre-determined percentages embedded within LPP.

The company’s wholly owned subsidiary, Insurance Administrative Services, LLC (IAS), performs claims administration on behalf of insurance partners and receives administrative fees representing a portion of the insurance premiums paid by automotive lenders. IAS ensures continuity of customer service and facilitates a seamless experience between LPP, insurance partners, and automotive lenders.

Loans facilitated through LPP are referred to as certified loans based on the date the loan is awarded to the consumer. Revenue is generated from program fees paid by automotive lenders for the use of LPP to underwrite loans, profit-sharing with insurance partners providing default insurance to automotive lenders, and fees paid by insurance partners for claims administration services. Claims management administration fees are typically calculated as 3% of monthly insurance earned premium for as long as a loan remains outstanding.

ApexOne Auto

On November 6, 2025, the company announced the launch of ApexOne Auto, an advanced decisioning platform that supports loans made to prime borrowers. Similar to LPP, ApexOne Auto uses risk-based pricing models to arrive at an all-inclusive interest rate for a loan that is customized to each automotive lender, reflecting cost of capital, loan servicing and acquisition costs, expected recovery rates, and target return on assets. Unlike loans facilitated through LPP, default insurance is not provided in connection with loans facilitated through ApexOne Auto.

Ecosystem

The company’s products enable the parties within its robust ecosystem to benefit from the ability to integrate with one another through its platform.

Automotive Lenders

The company’s customers include credit unions, regional banks, finance companies, and OEM captive finance companies. LPP customers rely on the company to assist in insuring against loan defaults by pairing them with highly rated insurance companies, which mitigate the added risk associated with lending to near-prime and non-prime borrowers. The company supports new and used automotive loans originated through various channels, including direct loans where the customer interfaces directly with the lender; indirect loans through networks of auto dealers who work with its lenders; and targeted refinance programs implemented by its lenders.

Insurance Partners

As of December 31, 2025, the company partners with three active insurance partners to provide auto loan default insurance policies for LPP-certified loans.

Borrowers

Through LPP, the company addresses the financing needs of borrowers with a credit bureau score generally between 560 and 699, referred to as consumers. It seeks to meet their specific needs by supporting lending opportunities through the use of LPP.

Government Regulation

State attorneys general, state licensing regulators, and state and local consumer protection offices, as well as federal agencies, such as the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, have authority to investigate consumer complaints and to commence investigations and other formal and informal proceedings regarding the company's operations and activities.

History

Open Lending Corporation was founded in 2000.

OSL Group Limited, an investment holding company, engages in digital assets and blockchain platform business in Hong Kong and Singapore.

Business Segments

The company operates through several distinct segments that cater to different aspects of the digital asset marketplace.

Brokerage Services

Brokerage Services segment provides institutional clients with end-to-end trading solutions, which include execution, settlement, and management of digital asset investments.

Custody Services

Custody Services segment is vital to the company's business model. With the increasing focus on security in the digital asset space, the company offers comprehensive custody solutions that are designed to safeguard assets from potential security threats. By leveraging advanced technology and best-in-class security protocols, the custodial services ensure the protection of clients' assets while offering ease of access and management.

Trading Platform

Trading Platform segment stands as a significant pillar of its operations, delivering an intuitive and effective trading experience for users. The platform supports a wide array of features, from algorithmic trading to customizable investment strategies, catering to both seasoned traders and novices. The integration of innovative tools and analytics enhances the trading experience, allowing clients to make informed decisions.

Business Strategy

The company’s business strategy centers on establishing the company as a leader in providing secure, compliant, and efficient trading of digital assets. To achieve this objective, the company focuses on robust technological infrastructure. By investing in cutting-edge technology, the company ensures that clients experience minimal latency and optimum reliability during trades, which is crucial in the fast-paced digital asset market.

In addition, the company aims to foster strategic partnerships within the industry to expand its service offerings and market presence. Collaborations with other tech firms, financial institutions, and regulatory bodies are essential for positioning itself as the preferred partner in the digital finance landscape.

Ultimately, the company’s strategic focus is on innovation and resilience, preparing to adapt quickly to shifts in market dynamics and consumer behaviors. Through a combination of resourceful planning, technological advancements, and a strong commitment to compliance, the company is poised to sustain its upward trajectory in the realm of digital assets.

Products and Services

The company develops an extensive range of products and services tailored to the demands of today's digital asset market. The primary product offering includes an advanced brokerage service that allows clients to trade a multitude of digital assets through a highly secure and compliant platform. This service is designed to cater to institutional clients, providing them with robust tools for executing large transactions efficiently and effectively.

In addition, the company offers custodial services critical for asset protection. As security remains a paramount concern in the cryptocurrency domain, the custodial solutions leverage state-of-the-art technology, including multi-signature wallets and Cold storage options, ensuring that digital assets are stored safely. These custodial offerings address both individual client needs and institutional requirements, facilitating trust in the management of high-value digital assets.

The company also operates an intuitive trading platform that incorporates comprehensive features to enhance the trading experience. Clients can access real-time market data, advanced charting tools, and risk management features that provide insights into trading strategies. The trading platform supports algorithmic trading, allowing advanced investors to implement custom trading strategies with precision.

Moreover, the company places an emphasis on educational services, aimed at informing and guiding clients through the complexities of investing in digital assets. The company has established a suite of educational programs, webinars, and resources designed to equip clients with the knowledge necessary to make informed investment decisions.

Seasonality

The company’s operations exhibit a degree of seasonality that is predominantly tied to market trends, including trading volumes and investment behaviors in the digital asset space. The company typically experiences increased trading activity during times of the year, which can align with global economic events or seasonal peaks in consumer interest for digital assets. To mitigate the effects of seasonality, the company continuously engages in strategic marketing and client outreach programs, aiming to sustain engagement and activity throughout the year.

Customers

The company serves a diverse clientele encompassing various customer categories ranging from institutional investors to high-net-worth individuals and retail customers. The robust service offerings cater to the unique needs of each category, facilitating comprehensive support throughout their digital asset journey.

Institutional customers, such as hedge funds and family offices, represent a significant segment due to their increased participation in the digital asset marketplace. Retail customers also form a critical part of the customer base, benefiting from user-friendly interfaces and educational resources aimed at promoting financial literacy in digital assets.

Modes of Sales and Marketing

The company utilizes a multi-faceted approach to sales and marketing, incorporating both traditional and digital strategies to reach its diverse customer base. The company emphasizes digital marketing efforts, leveraging search engine optimization, content marketing, and social media platforms to enhance brand visibility and attract target audiences.

Additionally, the company engages in relationship marketing, nurturing interpersonal connections with existing clients and potential investors. Personalized outreach, webinars, and engagement in industry events allow the company to strengthen relationships and promote its offerings effectively. The company's sales strategy is heavily reliant on educating clients about digital assets, which builds trust and confidence in its services.

Government Regulations

The company actively engages in maintaining transparency and accountability, implementing systems to monitor compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) regulations.

History

The company was founded in 2003. It was incorporated in 2011. The company was formerly known as BC Technology Group Limited and changed its name to OSL Group Limited in 2024.

records.Short Business Description: OTC Markets Group Inc. operates regulated markets for trading 12,000 U.S. and international securities.
records.Long Business Description:
OTC Markets Group Inc. (OTC Markets Group) provides trading, disclosure, and corporate services for the U.S. and global companies. The company facilitates efficient trading without the complexity associated with national securities exchange listings. OTC Markets Group operates several marketplace tiers, including the OTCQX Best Market, OTCQB Venture Market, and Pink Open Market. Additionally, it is a well-regarded provider of market data and corporate services, particularly catering to the needs of financial institutions, issuers, and investors.

Business Segments

OTC Markets Group's operations are broadly categorized into three principal business segments: Market Data Licensing, Corporate Services, and Information Services. Each segment is crucial to the holistic functioning of the company and contributes to its diverse revenue streams.

The Market Data Licensing segment involves the distribution and resale of financial data, analytics, and information services. OTC Markets Group provides structured market data, such as real-time quotes and historical information about securities, through various channels, including direct connectivity, extranet providers, and third-party redistributors. Subscribers can utilize this data for diverse purposes, including compliance, trading, and investor relations. The company works closely with third-party data redistributors to ensure broad dissemination and access to its market data.

The Corporate Services segment encompasses a range of solutions designed for issuers seeking to trade on OTC Markets. This segment includes the OTCQX Best Market, OTCQB Venture Market, and Pink Open Market. Each market tier offers different benefits, regulatory frameworks, and disclosure requirements, allowing companies of varying sizes and maturity levels to find a suitable trading environment. Furthermore, services such as the OTC Disclosure & News Service enable issuers to enhance their visibility and communication with investors through necessary disclosures, news releases, and direct engagement opportunities.

Finally, the Information Services segment provides analytical tools and reports that aid financial institutions and individual investors in making informed trading decisions. This segment also includes various subscription services that deliver curated market insights, enhancing the overall experience for users of the OTC Markets platform.

Business Strategy

OTC Markets Group's business strategy revolves around enhancing technology-enabled products and services tailored to the evolving needs of its customers and the marketplace. The company aims to provide innovative solutions that offer value while maintaining competitive pricing.

The company continuously explores opportunities for strategic alliances and partnerships with various financial institutions, data providers, and technology firms to broaden its service offerings. The company's focus on creating an effective blend of transparency and accessibility is fundamental to its strategy, ensuring that stakeholders can engage seamlessly in a regulated market environment.

OTC Markets Group also emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong reputation for reliability, compliance, and effective market operations. This is achieved through rigorous adherence to regulatory standards and the implementation of best practices in customer engagement and data security. The company invests in advanced technology to enhance its platform's efficiency, making it adaptable to changing market dynamics and users’ requirements.

Moreover, OTC Markets Group’s strategy includes a keen focus on international markets and attracting a diverse array of companies seeking to trade in an environment that offers lower regulatory burdens than traditional exchanges. This multi-faceted approach not only aids in expanding its customer base but also strengthens its competitive position in the global financial market landscape.

Products and Services

OTC Markets Group offers an extensive suite of products and services designed to meet the diverse needs of its customers. The company's offerings can be divided into three key categories: market data services, corporate services for issuers, and informational services targeted at investors.

In market data services, OTC Markets Group provides comprehensive data licenses that deliver real-time and historical information on a wide range of securities. This data is essential for financial institutions and investors, as it enables efficient trading and investment decision-making. The company's data products are available through various channels, including direct market access, integration with trading platforms, and distribution through several market data redistributors.

The corporate services segment focuses on facilitating trading and enhancing visibility for issuers. This includes specialized services like the OTC Disclosure & News Service, which helps companies publish important public disclosures and press releases. The OTCQX Best Market and OTCQB Venture Market are tailored market tiers offered by the company, each with unique benefits and listings standards that meet the needs of different types of companies.

Moreover, OTC Markets Group provides additional services such as Virtual Investor Conferences, enabling issuers to communicate with potential investors in an engaging online format. This level of engagement helps strengthen relations and build trust among stakeholders.

In addition to these products, the company offers informational services that include analytics tools and insights catering to institutional and retail investors. This segment equips users with comprehensive analytical resources critical for making informed trading decisions.

Geographical Markets Served

OTC Markets Group primarily serves the U.S. market but also extends its offerings to international companies and investors. By providing trading platforms for non-U.S. companies seeking access to American investors, it plays a crucial role in global capital markets.

Customers

The company serves a diverse range of customers, including public and private issuers, financial institutions, traders, and investors. While specific names of customers are not mentioned in the document, its Market Data Licensing and Corporate Services divisions serve a broad customer base comprising over 12,000 companies across different sectors.

Modes of Sales and Marketing, Marketing, Distribution Channels

The company's marketing and distribution channels are designed to ensure wide reach and effectiveness in promoting its products and services. OTC Markets Group employs a range of marketing strategies, including digital marketing, traditional advertising, and participation in industry conferences. records.Long Business Description:
Pakistan Stock Exchange Limited (PSX) is a stock exchange in Pakistan, providing a platform for the trading of securities, including equities, bonds, and derivatives. The company plays a crucial role in the capital market ecosystem, facilitating capital formation and investment opportunities for a diverse range of participants, including individual investors, institutional investors, and corporations.

The company’s operations encompass various segments, including the listing of companies, trading of securities, and providing market data and analytics. PSX is dedicated to maintaining high standards of corporate governance and compliance, ensuring that its operations align with international best practices.

Business Segments

The company operates through several key business segments that contribute to its overall functionality and service offerings. The primary segments include the Demerged Undertaking and the Continuing Undertaking, which were established following the Board of Directors' decision to demerge PSX’s real estate operations. The Demerged Undertaking is set to be merged with PSX Financial Services (Private) Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary formed for this purpose, while the Continuing Undertaking will remain with PSX. This strategic move aims to streamline operations and enhance focus on core business activities.

In addition to the structural changes, the company has made significant advancements in its Information Technology initiatives. These initiatives include changes to the quotation system to accommodate new Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) and the performance of underlying indices. The company has also configured the Government Ijarah Sukuk (IGS) listing model in record time, meeting the satisfaction of the Ministry of Finance. Furthermore, PSX has initiated work on a book-building system in collaboration with 1Link, which will facilitate automated payments by investors during Initial Public Offerings (IPOs).

Business Strategy

The company’s business strategy focuses on enhancing its market position and expanding its service offerings to meet the evolving needs of investors and issuers. The company aims to build a robust issuer pipeline by actively reaching out to potential issuers and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) for listing on the Main Board and the Growth Enterprise Market (GEM) Board. The company has approached over 200 companies for listing on the Main Board and more than 100 companies for the GEM Board, demonstrating its commitment to promoting capital formation through the stock exchange.

In addition to issuer outreach, the company has engaged with various Chambers of Commerce and Industry to foster collaboration and promote awareness of the benefits of listing on the exchange. The company has conducted numerous industry awareness sessions across the country, emphasizing the importance of capital markets in driving economic growth. The company also places a strong emphasis on investor education and awareness. Through its Financial Literacy Initiative, the company has organized a significant number of investor awareness sessions and webinars, guiding participants on various aspects of investing in the capital market.

Products and Services

The company offers a comprehensive range of products and services designed to cater to the diverse needs of its clients. The primary offerings include the trading of equities, bonds, and derivatives, providing investors with various investment options. The company facilitates the listing of companies on its exchange, enabling businesses to raise capital through public offerings.

In addition to traditional trading services, the company has introduced innovative products such as Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) and Sukuk, catering to the growing demand for diversified investment options. The company’s collaboration with 1Link to develop a book-building system for automated payments during IPOs further enhances its service offerings.

Customers

Sales and Marketing

Government Regulations

records.Short Business Description: Pinterest, Inc. operates as a visual search and discovery platform in the United States, Canada, Europe, and internationally.
records.Long Business Description:
Pinterest, Inc. (Pinterest) operates as an AI-powered visual search and discovery platform, positioned at the intersection of search, social, and commerce.

The company can be accessed through its mobile application or the web. People use Pinterest to find useful, relevant ideas—and then bring them to life. Users interact with the platform in dynamic, multi-session journeys to find inspiration, curate their latest look, plan their next project, and shop from great brands.

The unique, first-party, intent-based signal received from user actions on Pinterest helps power the AI-based recommendation systems that the company uses to surface relevant and engaging content to its users.

AI also plays a central role in how the company drives value for its advertisers, who come to Pinterest to reach the company’s users with high commercial intent. The inspiration-to-action journey on Pinterest aligns with the advertiser marketing funnel, allowing the company to help brands reach customers at every stage, from discovery to purchase, through digital ads.

Users and Platform

The company has 619 million monthly active users from around the world who come to Pinterest to find new ideas, curate and refine their tastes, and turn those ideas into reality. The company’s platform particularly resonates with women, who comprise roughly two-thirds of its total user base. In addition, the company’s platform also resonates with the younger generation, as Gen Z users represent over 50% of its user base. Geographically, the company has a diverse user set, representing over 100 countries globally.

Content on Pinterest comes from a variety of sources, including retailers, brands, creators, publishers, and users. The company acquires that content via a wide range of methods, including product catalog uploads, direct publishing, and user curation. Content formats include images that allow users to click into an idea to learn more, videos that provide the steps of an idea, collages that allow users to piece together different images into one, and products that brands and merchants upload from catalogs.

On Pinterest, users interact with several surfaces, each of which offers distinct functionalities and experiences. Users often move between these surfaces various times in a single session and across multiple sessions. Saving content and creating boards and collages are highly unique and beneficial to the company’s ecosystem. This curation activity generates signals across a network of many billions of associations between Pins, searches, boards, products, and users on the company’s platform. Together, these connections comprise the company’s valuable Taste Graph, and help it serve users even more relevant content recommendations.

Home Feed: When users open the Pinterest mobile application or navigate to www.pinterest.com, they are by default in their Home Feed, where they can discover Pins relevant to their tastes and interests in a scrolling format. As users interact with more content—through searching, saving, and curating—their Home Feed is designed to become even more representative of their interests.

Search Page: On the Search surface, users find Pins they are looking for by typing a query in the search bar. The search functionality allows users to see many relevant possibilities that are personalized for their individual taste and interests. Users often come to Pinterest with a vague idea of what they’re looking for, and use the company’s visual search functionality to narrow their focus. As such, over 90% of the company’s searches are unbranded.

Related Pins: Visual discovery on Pinterest also happens when a user taps on a Pin to learn more about an idea or image, and a feed of visually similar Pins is served beneath the tapped image. These related Pins help users springboard off a point of inspiration to explore deeper into an interest or narrow in on the perfect product. The company’s related pins surface is powered by its recommendation models that use computer vision, designed to identify products in the Pin, and show other relevant organic or ads content that the user might find valuable to their inspiration-to-action journey.

Boards: Users save and organize Pins onto virtual ‘boards.’ Boards often are labeled with topical categories like ‘Hawaiian vacation,’ ‘spring outfits,’ or ‘living room furniture,’ and are a collection of Pins that help users organize the vast amount of visual content that they interact with on the platform.

Flywheel

The company’s users often come to the platform to get inspiration for many of life’s moments, which can lead to discovering new products and brands. As a result, commercial content from brands, retailers, and advertisers is central to Pinterest. In-market consumers on Pinterest tend to be early in their journey toward a purchase decision, and do not yet know exactly what they want to purchase. Accordingly, they are open to discovering new products and brands on Pinterest, rather than merely navigating to brands they already know, as is common on traditional search engines and e-commerce platforms. This creates a unique flywheel where relevant ads can not only enhance the user experience, but also drive more value for advertisers in the form of increased views, clicks, and conversions.

Advertising System

Ad Formats

The company has a number of advertising products to help advertisers meet users across the full funnel, from upper funnel brand advertising to lower funnel performance advertising. Many of the company’s ad formats can be leveraged by advertisers across upper and lower funnel objectives. Additionally, many of these formats are enabled with mobile deep links, and/or direct link capabilities for a seamless, one-click handoff from an ad to the advertiser’s mobile app or webpage, and increasingly, in-app purchase experiences.

Standard ad: A static image used to showcase content in a simple vertical image format.

Video ad: Used by advertisers to capture attention and tell a story with a visually engaging format.

Shopping ad: Used by advertisers who wish to promote specific products in their catalogs to reach users who are deciding what to buy.

Carousel ad: Multiple static images or videos in one carousel, used by advertisers to showcase more than one image or video at a time.

Collection ad: Used by advertisers to display products in action with a hybrid format that mixes lifestyle imagery and video with featured products.

Interactive ad: Used by advertisers to engage with their users through interactive formats.

Premier Spotlight ad: Used by advertisers to showcase their latest product launch or seasonal moments with exclusive placements on the Pinterest Home Feed and search page.

Idea ad: Used by advertisers to tell a story that inspires their audience and encourages action.

Ad Auction

The vast majority of the company’s advertisers buy ads through an auction-based system. The company’s ad auction allows it to serve ads to users at relevant moments, while optimizing business outcomes for advertisers.

The company offers ads across both the upper and lower funnel. Upper funnel ‘brand’ revenue is billed when an advertiser optimizes an ad campaign around ‘brand’ objectives like impressions (‘CPM’) or video views (‘CPV’). Lower funnel revenue is billed when an advertiser optimizes an ad campaign around ‘performance’ objectives like clicks (‘CPC’), actions (‘CPA’), or conversion events (‘oCPM’), such as a checkout or add-to-cart.

The company’s auction system selects the best ad for each available ad impression, based on the likelihood of a desired action occurring, and how much that action is worth to advertisers. The likelihood of the action occurring depends on a variety of factors, such as ad relevance and creative quality.

records.Short Business Description: Prophecy DeFi Inc. invests in digital currencies, web3-related companies, and publicly traded securities in Canada.
records.Long Business Description:
Prophecy DeFi Inc. provides liquidity to decentralized cryptocurrency exchanges and receives digital currencies.

Business Segments

The company operates through segments: liquidity provisioning and investment income.

Liquidity Provisioning

This segment allows the company to act as a facilitator within the DeFi space, ensuring that sufficient liquidity is available for decentralized exchanges. By deploying digital assets into liquidity pools, the company plays a vital role in maintaining the fluidity of trading, hence enhancing user experience.

Investment Income

This segment derives profits from various forms of cryptocurrency, through either transactional sales or as rewards for participating in liquidity pools. The revenue recognition for these segments is meticulously calculated based on the fair value of the digital currencies involved, with all financial instruments being reported comprehensively to reflect the actual monetary values at various measurement periods.

Business Strategy

The company’s business centered around innovation, operational efficiency, and strategic partnerships. The company recognizes the importance of continuous adaptation to market changes, particularly within the fast-paced world of cryptocurrencies and DeFi applications.

The company’s strategy focuses on enhancing liquidity provision. The company strives to remain competitive by optimizing the assets allocated to various liquidity pools. This is achieved through advanced analytics and market trend assessments that inform decision-making.

The company emphasizes scalability as part of its business strategy. As the demand for DeFi solutions grows, the company is poised to scale its operations effectively, ensuring that it meets the increasing needs of the market while simultaneously managing risks.

Products and Services

The primary offerings of the company are centered around liquidity provisioning and digital asset management. As part of liquidity provisioning services, the company deploys digital currencies into various liquidity pools, thereby enhancing transaction capabilities on decentralized exchanges.

Additionally, the company’s digital asset management services focus on optimizing the performance of invested cryptocurrencies. The company engages in systematic analysis and investment strategies designed to yield positive returns through active management of its digital currency portfolio. By strategically buying and selling cryptocurrencies in response to market conditions, the company capitalizes on price fluctuations.

The company provides consulting and advisory services.

The integration of technology into these services enhances the company's ability to track and maintain its digital asset holdings, ensuring accurate reporting and risk management. By utilizing a robust tech infrastructure, the company offers transparency and real-time monitoring of its liquidity pools and asset management activities.

Customers

The company caters to a diverse clientele that spans various categories within the decentralized finance space. The primary customers include individual cryptocurrency traders, institutional investors, liquidity providers, and DeFi platforms that rely on robust liquidity provisioning services.

Modes of Sales and Marketing/ Marketing/Distribution Channels

The company employs a multifaceted approach to sales and marketing, which is vital to its success within the competitive decentralized finance landscape. To effectively reach its target audience, the company utilizes a combination of digital marketing strategies, content creation, partnerships, and participation in DeFi-related events.

Digital marketing plays a pivotal role, with the company leveraging online platforms to disseminate information about its liquidity provisioning services and investment capabilities. This is complemented by content creation efforts, including educational resources that inform potential clients about the dynamics and benefits of decentralized finance, thereby generating interest and engagement.

Strategic partnerships with key players in the DeFi ecosystem enhance the company’s visibility and credibility. Collaborating with established platforms and industry leaders facilitates access to a broader customer base and builds trust within the community.

Participation in blockchain and DeFi conferences also forms an integral part of the marketing strategy. These events provide valuable networking opportunities and allow the company to showcase its innovations and developments to an audience that is keenly interested in decentralized finance.

By employing a calculated blend of marketing and distribution channels, the company positions itself effectively within the decentralized finance market, fostering growth and engagement in its service offerings.

History

The company was formerly known as Bucephalus Capital Corp. and changed its name to Prophecy DeFi Inc. in 2021.
